The Battle of La Ventana was a confrontation between the royalist troops of the Amazonas and the patriots of Chachapoyas, which occurred on September 10, 1822.
Background
Following the proclamation of Maynas independence and its declaration of integration into the nascent Peruvian Republic, the Spanish remnants of the Amazonas, commanded by Santiago Cárdenas, left from Putumayo until they reached Moyobamba and took the city. Shooting the patriots who were there in the main square, among whom stood out Domingo de Alvariño, the patriotic governor of Maynas. From Moyobamba, Cárdenas left with a contingent of 1,000 royalist soldiers to take the cities of Chachapoyas and Cajamarca .
The battle
On the way to Chachapoyas, Commander Cárdenas met the patriotic expedition of Reaño and Arriola, who had orders to advance until recapturing Moyobamba for the patriotic side. The battle would take place in a place located eight leagues from the city, from where the immensity of the Mayo River could be seen.
The Spanish entrenched themselves in that place, but were eventually driven out by Reaño's men, who suffered only one casualty.
Consequences
This would be the first of a series of three battles that would see the defeat of Cárdenas' men in their attempt to advance towards Chachapoyas, who would finally be defeated in the Battle of Habana
